content:
incident-bot: Pager fired -> severity: P1. Reason: spike in TLS handshake failures from edge -> 1978723400s onward. pd:INC-7642

Maya (oncall): seeing the page now, joining. oncall handoff in 5m if needed.

Maya (oncall): alerting network team @Priya. Are you around? :wave:

Priya (network): here, grabbing logs from the ALBs and DNS provider. first glance looks like handshake errors from a subset of edge nodes.

Sam (prod-eng): getting stack traces from services — some clients reporting ECONNRESET during TLS handshake.

Maya (oncall): what fraction of traffic? metrics?

Arjun (sre): Grafana: TLS HANDSHAKE FAIL rate jumped from ~0.1% -> 8% at 08:12 UTC, correlated with increased 503 from target group A.

Priya (network): running `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:tg:A` now.

Priya (network): output (snippet):
```
Target: i-0abc1234  -> unhealthy (Reason: TLS handshake failed)
Target: i-0def5678  -> healthy
Target: i-0fed4321  -> unhealthy (Reason: TLS handshake failed)
```

Maya (oncall): confirmed customer-facing latency/errors on /api/generate during spike. CS alerted.

Sam (prod-eng): rolling diagnostics: may be a cert mismatch at LB->backend TLS. Backend cert rotated last night?

Arjun (sre): checking last deploys... no recent deploy to backend certs. last cert rotation was 4 days ago.

Priya (network): queried edge logs, showing SNI for some connections is empty or pointing to legacy-hostname.redwood-inference.internal. Looks like stale DNS entries at external resolver?

Maya (oncall): could be DNS propagation causing traffic to hit old LB with different cert bundle. If external resolvers still resolving old CNAME, clients might handshake against mismatched cert.

Priya (network): contacting DNS provider to check zones and TTL. Also running dig from multiple public resolvers.

Priya (network): dig results: some resolvers still return lb-old.example.net (CNAME -> old-ALB) with TTL ~300, others return lb-new.example.net.

Sam (prod-eng): that explains mixed behavior. Old ALB has different certificate chain (internal cert expired last week?). Need to confirm.

Arjun (sre): mitigation options: 1) drain old ALB targets quickly, 2) update old ALB cert to match current, 3) raise DNS TTL to force re-resolve? (raising TTL won't help immediate) 4) failover traffic by adjusting routing in fronting proxy (edge).

Maya (oncall): prioritize quick fix: drain old ALB targets so even if clients hit lb-old, they'll be routed to healthy targets that present correct cert. Priya, can we set target deregistration?

Priya (network): initiating target deregistration on old ALB target group now. Command: `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:tg:old --targets Id=i-0abc1234`

incident-bot: Action recorded: targets draining on old target group. Estimated complete: 2m.

Maya (oncall): Sam, confirm backend will accept plaintext or correct cert once traffic hits new targets.

Sam (prod-eng): backends have correct cert chain (deployed 4 days ago), but old ALB had fallback cert that failed handshake for some clients. Once drained, traffic should hit new ALB. Monitoring request success.

Priya (network): edge routing layer also supports a quick rule: prefer new ALB endpoints for TTL-stale clients. Applying weighted routing bias +15% -> new.

Arjun (sre): paging update: PagerDuty INC-7642 acknowledged by Maya at 08:14 UTC. Escalation to lead (Arjun) at 08:20 if not resolved.

pagerduty: Incident INC-7642 acknowledged by Maya (oncall).

Maya (oncall): CS: please hold customer comms, telling them we're mitigating a TLS handshake issue affecting a subset of requests. ETA: 10–15m for mitigation to take effect.

Priya (network): confirmed deregistration finished. Old targets show 0 healthy. Edge dig checks indicate more resolvers now returning lb-new.example.net.

Arjun (sre): metrics: TLS failures dropped from 8% -> 0.6% in last minute. 5xx count falling.

Sam (prod-eng): logs show successful TLS handshakes resuming, no spurious client cert issues.

Maya (oncall): keeping incident open while we monitor for 30m. Handoff note: if issue resurfaces, escalate to oncall lead.

Priya (network): follow-up: DNS provider confirms stale cache at a handful of public resolvers; TTL for the change was 300s so full propagation may take up to 5m per resolver. They cleared some caches on request.

Sam (prod-eng): suggestion for postmortem: root cause seems to be a previously-deployed legacy ALB still present in zone with mismatched cert; DNS switch left some resolvers pointing to it. Need automation to detect orphaned/legacy LBs before cutover.

Arjun (sre): agreed. Action items: (a) add pre-cutover checks for legacy endpoints, (b) add an automated drain-and-retire step, (c) monitor TLS handshake rate post-cutover for 60m.

Maya (oncall): PRs to track: Priya -> dns/cleanup automation; Sam -> deployment gating check; Arjun -> alert tuning and runbook updates.

pagerduty: Incident INC-7642 status changed to monitoring.

Maya (oncall): marking official mitigation: drained old targets + routing bias applied. Customer impact: transient TLS handshake failures, small percentage of requests during 08:12–08:18 UTC. No data loss.

Priya (network): will follow up with DNS provider to request TTL reduction guidance for future cutovers.

Sam (prod-eng): adding logs & graphs to the incident doc.

Maya (oncall): wrapping up. If anyone sees uptick, ping same thread. Thanks all. :heart:

Arjun (sre): thanks — filing postmortem draft.

incident-bot: Thread closed for now; monitoring window active until 08:48 UTC.
